Validate paper.yaml, targets.yaml and consistency.yaml against the rubric. Without --final, undecided outcomes and reviews are warnings; with --final everything must be decided and audit.json current, as seal requires, and:

```sh
the report  is final, its scorecard, findings, reproduced results and
            comparison with other audits are drawn from this audit.json, it
            has a summary, a section for every result that differs and names
            every skipped one, it is safe (UTF-8, only storyteller's scripts,
            nothing loaded from outside the file), and its PDF (beside it,
            from storyteller pdf) was printed after its last change
the pipeline  is packed, every parameter in its workflow/config.yaml has a
            comment saying where it comes from, and every result a target
            gives as evidence is one it writes (expected/checksums.tsv)
the plan    in Roots, where codeflower-roots is here: no line of work is
            still active or blocked, and the report shows the plan
the review  before sealing is recorded (codeflower-audit review): every item
            of its checklist has a status, and audit.json, the report and
            the pipeline archive have not changed since
```

Warnings do not stop a seal, but each is a question to answer first: an exact or close outcome its values do not support, a reported value with nothing reproduced under its name, an assumption no result relies on, a revision or dissent not recorded as an intervention.


## Usage

```sh
codeflower audit check [flags]
```

## Flags

| Flag | Default | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `--dir string` | `audit` | the audit folder (paper.yaml, targets.yaml, consistency.yaml) |
| `--final` |  | everything must be decided, scored, in the report and packed |
